name: zboy
why: A Game Boy emulator is familiar territory, but running old handheld ROMs in a terminal-adjacent setup still has a bit of charm.

brief.what_it_is: zBoy is a multi-platform, open-source emulator for the GameBoy Classic (DMG) handheld, written by Mateusz Viste. It loads ROM files and plays them with keyboard, joypad, or both. It can save and load game state, take PCX screenshots, and emulate the battery for ROMs that were built with one. It can also scale the video output with Scale2x or Scale3x.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit problem statement. It presents zBoy as a feature-rich open-source alternative that adds things many emulators lack, such as LAN two-player link play and hi-score saving for games that cannot save their own tables.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage describes features but not internals. It says zBoy emulates a link between two consoles so two players can play over LAN, and that it intelligently saves hi-scores for cartridges with no battery-backed RAM. It does not explain how either is implemented.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no install steps beyond pointing to a 'Download files here' link and a separate page for pre-compiled Linux packages. It says the emulator runs on Linux, DOS and Windows and should compile on other systems. No runtime, account, or configuration requirements are stated. The site also offers a public domain game pack for testing, since no commercial ROMs are included.
brief.standout: It is one of the very few GameBoy emulators that support two-player play over LAN, emulating the link cable between two consoles. It also keeps old DOS support alive alongside Linux and Windows, and it reconstructs hi-score saving for games that never had battery RAM.
brief.status: Quiet, as far as the homepage shows. The copyright line reads 2010-2020, which is the newest date visible. The page shows no release version, release date, or repository activity, so the current state is unconfirmed. No repository link was given and I did not follow the download links.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not ship any games, and the author says so. Commercial ROMs must be sourced separately, and the page points only to public domain test ROMs. Platform support is listed as Linux, DOS and Windows, with other systems only expected to compile. The page does not describe a terminal interface, so the scout note's terminal-adjacent framing is not supported by this source. The page also says nothing about licensing terms beyond the copyright notice.
quotes: zBoy is a multi-platform, open-source GameBoy Classic ("DMG") emulator that provides a load/save feature, can perform PCX screenshots and emulates an internal battery for ROMs that were designed to use one.
It is also one of the very few emulators that make it possible to play games in 2-players mode over LAN, emulating a link between two consoles.
The zBoy emulator is not, and will not be shipped with any actual GameBoy game.
fetch_log: https://zboy.sourceforge.net/ - fetched OK; HTML page, not a GitHub repo, so no README. Its text is descriptive but has no command lines and no install instructions. The download and Linux package links were present only as labels, with no URLs in the extracted text, so I did not follow them.

judge.reason: LAN link-cable play and hi-score reconstruction make this obscure Game Boy emulator more than another way to run familiar ROMs.

entry.title: zBoy
entry.tldr: A small open-source Game Boy emulator that can link two virtual consoles over a LAN and rebuild hi-score tables for games with no battery save.
entry.deeper_look:
zBoy is an emulator for the original Game Boy (the DMG model), written by Mateusz Viste. It loads ROM files and plays them with keyboard, joypad, or both. It can save and load game state, take PCX screenshots, and emulate the battery-backed memory in cartridges that had one. Video can be scaled with Scale2x or Scale3x.

Two features set it apart. It emulates the link cable between two consoles, so two players can play head to head over a LAN. It also saves hi-scores for games that never had battery RAM and so could never keep their own tables. The homepage describes both features but not how they are implemented, so the internals are yours to find out.

The idea underneath is that a handheld from 1989 is a small, well-bounded machine, and emulating it is a good way to learn how hardware gets recreated in software. A link cable is a serial connection, and carrying it over a network shows how a physical protocol can be turned into packets.

zBoy ships no games, and the author says so. The site points to a public domain game pack for testing.
entry.install:
brew install zboy

This pulls in sdl2-compat. You supply your own ROM files. The homepage offers a public domain game pack for testing.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the available options, a starting point for loading a ROM and choosing scaling or controls.

entry.whats_unique: It is one of the very few Game Boy emulators that emulate the link cable for two-player play over LAN. It also reconstructs hi-score saving for games with no battery RAM.
entry.caveats: The homepage shows a copyright line of 2010-2020 and no release version or repository activity, so the current state is unconfirmed, and it does not describe a terminal interface.
